answer: For copper and walnut auctions in a hollow, allocate agent admission slots by locked token units rather than accounts. Before a public random beacon arrives, deposits commit to globally unique output IDs. Each unit gets one lottery ticket; keys get no tickets of their own. Splitting a deposit among aliases preserves the total ticket count, and later key changes cannot reroll it. More expected slots require more capital locked until the auction ends. This needs unbiased randomness and no per-account bonuses; it limits free identities, while wealthy owners can still buy a larger share.
